SELF.glyph: A large open circle, drawn in a line of even weight, sits centred and whole: the still centre and the mandala of wholeness. Inside it, four small solid squares are placed at the four compass points, evenly spaced and touching the inner rim, the quaternity that gathers around the core. At the exact centre a single filled dot rests, the self that all else orbits; it is connected to each of the four squares by four short straight spokes of medium weight, so the interior reads as convergence. A second, thinner circle sits just outside the first, incomplete, broken at the top by a small gap: the opening through which the quiet light is let in and the individuation that never closes. One short horizontal bar of heavier weight crosses the gap, standing apart from both circles, the inner voice that speaks across the break. The composition is concentric and balanced, the heavy dot and squares anchoring the thin rings.

SHADOW.glyph: A large solid black disc sits at the centre-right, heavy and closed, the disowned mass that refuses light. A second disc of the same size, hollow with a single thick outline, overlaps it to the left and sits slightly lower, its rim crossing into the filled disc: the twin opposite that follows behind and cannot be separated. Where the two discs overlap, a slim crescent of white is cut cleanly out of the filled disc along the hollow one's inner edge, a sliver of gold buried in the mass. From the hollow disc's lower-left rim a single straight line drops downward and stops short, unattached, the dread that creeps without arriving. Around the hollow disc's outer edge, three short bars stand apart at even spacing, refused confessions held at a distance. The filled disc carries no bars and no lines leaving it; everything gathers toward it and stays.

ANIMA.glyph: A tall solid lens stands off-centre to the right, slightly tilted, its mass dense and closed: the soul image, held and unreachable. A thin continuous line enters from the left edge, runs toward the lens and stops short of it, a short gap before the surface: the bridge inward that never quite lands. Along that line three small hollow circles sit at even intervals, feelings surfacing in the dark. From the lens's upper tip a single open curve rises and curls back toward itself without closing, a beckoning that returns to its own source. Below, a wide shallow arc opens downward, cupping empty space beneath the lens, what is veiled and withheld. A single filled dot rests apart at the lower left, the unfamiliar familiar, drawn but not yet joined.

ANIMUS.glyph: A tall narrow upright bar, solid and heavy, stands slightly left of centre: the animus as conviction, unmoving and self-certain. It is cut by a single horizontal gap near its lower third, so the mass reads as two stacked blocks barely meeting: the inner argument that will not close. From the top of the bar a thin line rises straight, then bends sharply once to the right and thins away: the unbidden opinion that arrives and will not return. To the right, a hollow open curve arcs from low to high, its ends curling inward without touching, a vessel that never quite encloses: the guide that stands beside but is not held. A single dot floats in the gap between the bar and the curve's inner edge, level with the bar's cut: the bridge point where the two almost meet. Below the curve's lower end, three short parallel bars lie flat and evenly spaced, thin and separate: the repeated voices heard and set down.

PERSONA.glyph: A large hollow oval stands upright at the centre, slightly taller than wide, its outline a single unbroken stroke: the public face, closed and continuous, presenting one clean edge. Inside it, offset to the left, sits a smaller solid black oval of about half its height, the hidden face held within the show. A thin vertical bar crosses the hollow oval just above the solid one and continues a little past the outer stroke at the top, a borrowed voice running through. Along the lower right outer edge of the hollow oval, three short parallel bars cross the outline at even intervals, the rhythm of fitting in. To the left of the hollow oval, standing apart, a short thick bar leans at a slight tilt, the polite smile worn at an angle. From the lower right of the hollow oval a thin line runs outward and stops short, not touching a small dot beyond it: the door left ajar, the way out kept open. The whole composition sits slightly off centre, tilted a few degrees, balance deliberately unsettled.

HERO.glyph: A thick vertical bar stands slightly left of centre, its top cut flat, its base widening into a heavy foot: the fixed resolve that holds against pressure. A second thinner bar leans toward it from the right at a shallow angle, its upper end stopping short of the first, the approach of the call and the struggle closing in. Between the two bars, near their upper thirds, a small solid square floats free, not touching either: the wound carried at the centre of the crossing. Below the bars a single unbroken curve sweeps from the left edge under both and rises toward the right, thinning as it goes: the journey out and the road home. A short open arc cups the base of the thick bar from underneath, not touching it, the threshold that must be crossed and re-crossed. Three small dots sit in a diagonal from the square down toward the thin bar, each smaller than the last: the resolve that scatters and reforms.

WISE OLD MAN.glyph: A large open circle, drawn with a heavy even stroke, sits at the centre and holds nothing inside but empty space: the cave, the patient silence that contains rather than fills. Inside it, offset toward the lower left, a small solid dot rests like a seed of counsel held in stillness. From the top of the circle a single thick vertical bar rises a short distance and stops flat, like an old root that no longer grows: the ancient eyes fixed on what is above. Two thin curved lines leave the circle at the lower right, diverging as they fall away and thinning to nothing, a guiding hand that reaches out and releases. Around the upper right of the circle, three short parallel strokes arc with the circle's edge at even spacing, a rhythm of slow repeated light: the lantern's patient glow. A second smaller open circle, drawn lighter, sits at the lower left just touching the great circle from outside, the inner teacher standing apart yet adjacent. The whole tilts very slightly to the left, the weight of years leaning toward the held dot.

GREAT MOTHER.glyph: A large hollow circle, open at the top, dominates the upper two thirds of the field: the embracing enclosure that shelters but also swallows, its gap letting light and air in. Inside it, at its lowest point, a solid black disc sits heavy and closed, the womb-dark core that draws everything down. Two thick curved bars descend from the rim's opening toward the disc, thick and unbroken, like arms that cradle and bind; they do not touch the disc, leaving a thin gap. Below the circle, a single long horizontal line runs the full width, the ground that holds the whole; a second shorter line sits just under it, doubled rhythm of rootedness. A small solid wedge, point up, is set in the gap between the two bars and the disc, caught between embrace and descent. The whole is tilted very slightly, so the circle leans left, unsettled comfort.

TRICKSTER.glyph: A thick black bar runs horizontally across the upper third, continuous and heavy: the rule that everything must pass through. At its centre the bar is broken by a narrow gap, and through the gap a thin line slips downward, bending once sharply to the left then once to the right, a path that reverses direction twice before ending in a small filled dot just below the bar's level: the crossing and the sudden turn. On the right, a short bar stands vertically, tilted a few degrees off true, touching neither the long bar nor the dot: the sacred fool who stands apart from order. On the left, a hollow open curve loops back on itself in a nearly closed circle, its two ends overlapping without meeting, sitting above the long bar: laughter and masks, a shape that contains and conceals but never seals. A single small dot rests inside the hollow curve, off-centre. Below the long bar, well separated, three short parallel strokes lie flat at slight angles to one another, none aligned with the bar: chaos, the rhythm that will not settle. The composition is deliberately off-balance, weighted toward the left loop and the right tilted bar, with the centre gap as the only point of symmetry.
